Quantization在多仓同步推进MoE专家FP4量化路径优化，调整fallback优先级以减少仿真开销、提升吞吐。

## Motivation

Addresses the DSpark RoPE boundary defect discussed in #33454 and the H100 report in #53092. The incident did not capture the failing position tensor. The source defect is independently covered by a regression test.

items.title: [Fix] Wake waiting readers when a queued writer is cancelled in RWLock.acquire_writer
items.author: deep1blue
items.summary: In, enforces writer-preference fairness by blocking in. When a waiting writer coroutine in is cancelled while blocked on, the block decrements without notifying.
items.body:
## Summary

In `python/sglang/srt/utils/aio_rwlock.py` (`RWLock`), `acquire_reader()` enforces writer-preference fairness by blocking in `while self._writer_active or self._waiting_writers > 0: await self._cond.wait()`.

When a waiting writer coroutine in `acquire_writer()` is cancelled (`asyncio.CancelledError`) while blocked on `await self._cond.wait()`, the `finally:` block decrements `self._waiting_writers -= 1` without notifying `self._cond`. As a result, when the last waiting writer is cancelled and `self._waiting_writers` drops to `0` while `not self._writer_active`:

items.author: phphlio1

## Motivation

Fixes #41317. The DeepSeek DSML detectors strip the value of every `string="true"` parameter, so leading and trailing whitespace that belongs to the argument is lost. - `--tool-call-parser deepseekv32` on all endpoints.

items.body:
## Overview

Looped models run their shared-weight layers more than once per forward pass, with a KV cache per pass: the attention module adds an offset argument to `self.layer_idx` for the cache layer it writes. The Transformers backend creates one vLLM attention layer per attention module, so all passes share one KV cache and the output is wrong from the second forward pass on, without an error. This PR creates one attention layer per cache layer and gives each call its own.

items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: Routed experts capture rejected pipeline parallelism, because each stage captures only its own MoE layers while TP rank 0 of the last stage returns every layer. With routed experts enabled, a non-first stage now receives the earlier stages' rows as a intermedi…
items.body:
Stacked on #57968 (which is stacked on #62920). **Review the last commit only.**

## Summary

Routed experts capture rejected pipeline parallelism, because each stage captures only its own MoE layers while TP rank 0 of the last stage returns every layer. With routed experts enabled, a non-first stage now receives the earlier stages' rows as a `routed_experts` intermediate tensor (as `PPHandler` relays positions) and its forward overwrites its own layers. The tensor is not split across TP ranks. The last stage's buffer then holds every layer, so the output path and object writes are unchanged.

items.summary: Adds an opt-in fused FP32 Triton kernel on ROCm that combines LayerNorm, scale/shift, and residual/gate into a single pass for Wan diffusion inference, replacing the multi-kernel BF16 fallback path.
items.body:
## Motivation

**What**
Add an opt-in ROCm Triton kernel, `rocm_norm_scale_shift` (`SGLANG_ROCM_TRITON_NORM_SCALE_SHIFT=true`), that fuses residual + gate, LayerNorm and scale/shift for Wan in one pass, and call it from `_ScaleResidualNormScaleShift` and `_NormScaleShift` on ROCm.

**Why**
On ROCm the Wan norm and modulation fall back to native torch ops, which run several kernels and round to BF16 in between, while the CUDA fused kernels compute in FP32 and round once. The Triton kernel follows the CUDA contract (FP32 compute, BF16 storage) in a single kernel.

**Status: draft, default off.**

items.body:
## Overview

On ROCm, an incremental build after editing a header under `csrc/` compiles nothing; only the build after that one recompiles the objects that include the header. items.title: [Fix] disaggregation: Hold the status lock while clear() pops a room
items.author: ShangmingCai
items.summary: Fixes a race condition in disaggregated serving where clear pops bootstrap rooms without holding _status_lock, allowing stale status writes to resurrect rooms.
items.body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #52976. `update_status` now does its read-modify-write under `_status_lock`, but `CommonKVSender.clear()` and `CommonKVReceiver._clear()` still pop the room without it. A worker, status-receiver, or bootstrap control thread that has already read a non-None status can write back after the pop and resurrect the room. A later request that reuses the same `bootstrap_room` (decode retraction / recompute) then sees a non-None opening status, keeps the stale value via `max()`, and skips the reset of deferred-ACK, staging, and send-record state. Flagged by the review bot on
discussion: @claude review

items.author: ex25
items.summary: In, and copy the query's in two places: 1. For a 32K-token query, both a full hit and a first-page miss pay for a 256 KiB copy, even though tree edges are already page-aligned and rounds down to whole pages.
items.body:
## Motivation

items.summary: builds a 1-head dummy query to skip full-Q work when applying RoPE to the draft's keys. The rotary kernel checks; a 1-head makes, which fails whenever per rank is > 1.

## Motivation

`DSparkMiniMaxAttention.apply_k_rope` builds a **1-head** dummy query to skip full-Q work when applying RoPE to the draft's keys. The rotary kernel checks `num_q_heads % num_kv_heads == 0`; a 1-head `dummy_q` makes `num_q_heads = 1`, which fails whenever `num_kv_heads` per rank is > 1. Serving `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` with the DSpark draft on **TP=2** aborts on the first speculative prefill:

```
File ".../sglang/srt/models/dspark.py", in write_target_hidden_kv
    k = attn.apply_k_rope(positions, k)
RuntimeError: Expected num_heads % num_kv_heads == 0 to be true, but got false.
```

`CommonKVManager.update_status` reads a room's status and writes the new one without a lock. On prefill, two threads open the same room:

When decode's metadata lands while prefill is still creating the sender, both threads read "room absent". If the `Bootstrapping` write comes last, it overwrites `WaitingForInput`. The sender then polls `Bootstrapping` forever, nothing re-sends decode's metadata, and the reques

## Description

## Motivation

Each TP group ends up holding two NCCL/RCCL communicators per GPU on the same ranks. PyNccl builds one at startup, then disables itself outside CUDA graph capture. The first eager collective on the group (the logits all-gather of the first prefill, or the sampler's grammar sync) goes through `torch.distributed` on `device_group`, and torch lazily builds a second communicator. That happens after the KV cache has been sized, so its buffers come out of the activation headroom.

With `--enable-unified-memory`, the full-attention and sliding-window (SWA) KV pages live in one arena and grow from its two ends, sharing the free room between them. items.author: hnyls2002
items.summary: With, a stream that delivers one token per chunk loses every tool call after the first. Intern-S1 tokenizes and as separate tokens, so the start marker of call 2 arrives over several chunks. [Discussion: /rerun-test teststreamingchunkboundaries.py]
items.body:
With `--tool-call-parser interns1`, a stream that delivers one token per chunk loses every tool call after the first. Intern-S1 tokenizes `<|action_start|>` and `<|plugin|>` as separate tokens, so the start marker `<|action_start|> <|plugin|>` of call 2 arrives over several chunks. Once a call had been emitted, `InternlmDetector.parse_streaming_increment` cleared any buffer without the full marker, so the first half of the marker was dropped and call 2 never parsed. Fixes #46661.

items.title: [fsdp] fix: use actual chunk count for TiledMLP last-shard gradient write-back
items.author: four1er
items.summary: Fixes #8839 dropped parameter gradients accumulated by earlier micro-batches whenever returned fewer chunks than (e.g. moves any existing into its buffer and writes it back only from the hook installed with, and never fired in that case, so the accumulated gra…
items.body:
Fixes #8839

`TiledMLP.backward` dropped parameter gradients accumulated by earlier micro-batches whenever `torch.chunk` returned fewer chunks than `num_shards` (e.g. `n=9, shards=4` gives 3 chunks of 3). `GradientAccumulator` moves any existing `param.grad` into its buffer and writes it back only from the hook installed with `is_last_shard=True`, and `is_last_shard = i + 1 == shards` never fired in that case, so the accumulated gradients were silently lost.

This PR uses the actual chunk count (`len(x_shards)`) for the last-shard test, so the write-back hook always fires on the final shard.

items.title: [Feat] diffusion/minimax-h3: Add a converter to native QKV layout
items.author: WellyXY
items.summary: H3's released transformers interleave the Q, K and V rows of each attention head. reorders them at load, so the fused QKV weights become an anonymous host copy (52 layers × 21504 × 5376 × 2 bytes = 11.2 GiB) that the page cache cannot drop.
items.body:
## Motivation

H3's released transformers interleave the Q, K and V rows of each attention head. `_install_qkv_weight_loader` reorders them at load, so the fused QKV weights become an anonymous host copy (52 layers × 21504 × 5376 × 2 bytes = 11.2 GiB) that the page cache cannot drop. On a 24 GB card with a 32 GiB host that copy is what keeps two H3 servers from fitting (#52762).

SGLang already supports the native layout through `checkpoint_qkv_layout: native`. This PR adds the offline conversion that produces it, so the DiT can stay on the file mapping. It changes no runtime code.

### What happens

`TiledMLP.backward` (`verl/models/transformers/tiled_mlp.py`) drops the parameter gradients that earlier micro-batches accumulated in `param.grad` whenever `torch.chunk` returns fewer chunks than `num_shards`.

`GradientAccumulator.__init__` moves any existing `param.grad` into its buffer and sets `param.grad = None`. The buffer is written back only by the hook installed with `is_last_shard=True`, and `is_last_shard = i + 1 == shards`. `torch.chunk(x, shards)` returns `ceil(n / ceil(n / shards))` chunks, which is fewer than `shards` for some `n` (for example `n = 9, shards =
discussion:

items.title: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] Add SM100 TP=4 skinny GEMM plans for the router and LM head
items.author: Johnsonms
items.summary: On B200 (SM100), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's low-latency decode GEMM table has the MoE router and the TP=4 LM head at M=1 only. 2- and 8-token decode batches therefore run both through cuBLAS split-K ( + ). [Discussion: Will you do any more small GEMM tuning?]
items.body:
## Overview

On B200 (SM100), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's low-latency decode GEMM table (`QWEN4_EXP_SM100_GEMM_PLANS`, `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/low_latency_gemm.py`) has the MoE router `(512, 2560)` and the TP=4 LM head `(62080, 2560)` at M=1 only. 2- and 8-token decode batches therefore run both through cuBLAS split-K (`nvjet_*_splitK` + `cublasLt::splitKreduce_kernel`). This PR adds B200-measured cuteDSL skinny-GEMM plans for the router at M=2/8 and the LM head at M=2, and retunes the LM head's M=1 entry. Table-only, SM100 only, +8/−5 lines. Follow-up to #59214 (SM100 TP=4 plans) and #64482
discussion: Will you do any more small GEMM tuning? If yes, can you fold them into a single PR?
Yes, a few more are likely. I'll fold #69743, #69773 and this one into #69736 and close the others, and add any further small-GEMM tuning there instead of opening new PRs.

items.title: [Perf] mxfp4: Always pass the finalized output shape to deferred MoE calls above 32 rows
items.author: YAMY1234
items.summary: FlashInfer keys its trtllm-gen MoE tactic cache on the output shape. An MXFP4 MoE call with a deferred finalize passed the finalized output shape only at 97-384 rows.
items.body:
## Motivation

FlashInfer keys its trtllm-gen MoE tactic cache on the output shape. An MXFP4 MoE call with a deferred finalize passed the finalized output shape only at 97-384 rows. At 33-96 rows it passed the `(M, 0)` placeholder, so those calls missed the tuned tactic and ran the default one. #45450 added `SGLANG_OPT_MXFP4_DEFERRED_FINALIZED_SHAPE` to pass the finalized shape above 32 rows, behind a switch that `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION` also turns on (#47105). The change does not depend on the megakernel plugin, so this PR makes it the only path and removes the switch.

## Overview

When vLLM preempts a DiffusionGemma request, it drops the unfinished block. The request starts the block again from noise after prefill. The new `canvas_swap_capacity` option keeps the block on the GPU so denoising can resume. The default is `0` (off).

items.author: alphabetc1
items.summary: splits each pool's keys for a layer group into exactly ranged gets. A read therefore grows with the load batch, and a Mooncake ranged get slows down superlinearly in its range count.

## Motivation

`MooncakeDirectLinker._range_get_reads` splits each pool's keys for a layer group into exactly `linker_load_threads` ranged gets. A read therefore grows with the load batch, and a Mooncake ranged get slows down superlinearly in its range count. With long cached prefixes, a prefill batch can load 20 GB or more per rank, and those loads run at less than half the bandwidth of smaller ones.

## Overview

`LMCacheMPConnectorUpstream.request_finished` always returned `True`, so an abort during a KV load looked like an in-flight save. The worker then reported `finished_sending` for that request after the scheduler had freed it, and `assert req_id in self.requests` killed EngineCore.

Fixes the bundled-connector half of #69137. Same failure shape as #46240 and #56089. The external LMCache connector was fixed in LMCache/LMCache#5938; this is the in-tree fallback, which still returned `True` unconditionally.

### Feature request

For hybrid models (Qwen3.5, Qwen3-Next) on the SGLang rollout, hold each prompt's prefix state with an SGLang session (`--enable-session-radix-cache`, sglang >= 0.5.17, sgl-project/sglang#29173) until all samples of that prompt are done, then close the session.

### Motivation

A hybrid model can reuse a cached prefix only if the recurrent (Mamba) state at its end is still in SGLang's fixed-size state pool, which is evicted by LRU. With many prompts in flight, the prompts' states are the oldest and go first, so later samples of the same prompt recompute the whole prompt.

`_call_once` logs with brace formatting, but `logger` is a stdlib `logging.getLogger(__name__)`, which interpolates with `%`:

## Motivation

On systems where GPUs on several nodes share one NVLink domain, a prefill server's HiCache L3 can live in **host memory of other nodes in that domain**, for example the decode nodes of a PD deployment, whose host memory is mostly idle. With CUDA fabric handles, the prefill GPUs read and write that memory directly over NVLink with their copy engines. No NIC, no RDMA transfer engine and no CPU on the data path.

The existing L3 backends either use local storage (file, 3FS, ...) or an RDMA/TCP transfer engine (Mooncake, NIXL, ...). They do not use this NVLink host-memory path.

items.author: gchinora

items.body:
## Overview

A synchronous UMBP load (`load_async=false`) could be wiped by vLLM's own block zeroing. On a KV cache that needs zeroing, the runner queues the zeroing of the request's new blocks on the forward stream and then issues the load, and MORI's small-fragment copy is not ordered behind that stream. This PR keeps the blocks a synchronous load fills out of that step's zeroing list. MoRIIO does the same for its hybrid READs (#59164; #67074, open, extends it to mixed precision), and core does it for asynchronous loads (#59504). No wait is added.

## Summary

Fix Nemotron Shortcut's bucketed refits and make video preprocessing match the training format. Still-image sizes continue to come from the checkpoint's HF processor, with explicit overrides preserved.

## Why and how

**Bucketed refits:** after the sparse model has loaded its indexer, a later weight bucket containing only attention or MLP weights is incorrectly rejected for having no indexer weights. Remember successful initial validation across subsequent buckets. An initial sparse checkpoint without indexer weights is still rejected.

**T=1 video prompts:** individually encoded

The non-fused dense FSDP output path (`use_remove_padding=False`) narrows logits to valid sequence lengths and concatenates them into a second `[total_valid_tokens, vocab]` tensor before computing token log-probabilities. items.title: [#21809][fix] Reject MPI-disabled DeepEP bootstrap
items.author: Hang-get
items.summary: Ray workers set, but the DeepEP buffer wrappers still build their communicator from an MPI split. DeepEP's buffer constructor uses that communicator's rank count, so the low-latency strategy can initialize a one-rank buffer for a multi-rank EP mapping.
items.body:
## Description

Ray workers set `TLLM_DISABLE_MPI=1`, but the DeepEP buffer wrappers still build their communicator from an MPI split. DeepEP's buffer constructor uses that communicator's rank count, so the low-latency strategy can initialize a one-rank buffer for a multi-rank EP mapping. Normal DeepEP is usually rejected earlier by its local-MPI feasibility check.

Reject both strategies before platform probing or buffer allocation when MPI is disabled. AUTO selection can then continue through its existing fallback; forcing either strategy reports that its bootstrap requires MPI and does not

items.author: layahaasini
items.summary: When a TransferQueue put misses its data-status ACK (, 30s by default), TQ only logs it, so the controller never marks those samples ready. The next read through then gets an empty, again with just a warning.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8768.

When a TransferQueue put misses its data-status ACK (`TQ_DATA_UPDATE_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT`, 30s by default), TQ only logs it, so the controller never marks those samples ready. The next read through `tqbridge` then gets an empty `TensorDict`, again with just a warning. Training finally dies somewhere unrelated, e.g. `KeyError: 'loss_mask'` in `compute_log_prob`, which is hard to trace back to TQ.

items.body:
Fixes #9713

## Bug

Rank 0 rewrote `latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt` with `open(..., 'w')` and `latest_train_state.pt` with `shutil.copy`, both in place, so a crash mid-save could leave an empty tracker behind. On restart `read_metadata` then printed `ERROR: Invalid metadata file ... Exiting` and called bare `sys.exit()`, exiting 0, so the job ended without training and a scheduler took it as success. With `--save-retain-interval` an empty tracker also failed every later save with a bare `int()` `ValueError`.

## Fix

- `megatron/training/checkpointing.py`: new `write_text_file_atomically()

items.title: [https://nvbugs/7094481][fix] Stop busy-polling in the trtllm-bench async client
items.author: chenfeiz0326
items.summary: Fixes GIL starvation in trtllm-bench's async client by replacing busy-polling with an event-based wait, eliminating late request submission on dual-socket Intel hosts.
items.body:
## Description

trtllm-bench's async client dispatches its whole inbox into request tasks when the benchmark starts. For the rest of the run, `LlmManager.worker` then polled the empty inbox with `await asyncio.sleep(0)`, so the event loop never blocked: the client process kept a core busy and held the GIL most of the time. The LLM API thread that delivers each response to the request coroutines needs the GIL too.

On two-socket Intel hosts with Linux 5.15, like QA's H100 nodes, this starves that thread. CPython restarts a waiting thread's 5 ms switch timeout every time the GIL holder releases

items.body:
Continues #8915, which was closed automatically when its base branch was deleted after #9005 merged.

## What does this PR do?

items.body:
## Summary

On the V1 FSDP path, `update_weights` (actor → rollout engine weight sync) broadcasts the **full parameter set every training step**. Measured cost on Qwen2.5-32B TP8: ~9 s/step, every step, regardless of how few parameters changed. Over hundreds of GRPO steps this is a fixed tax proportional to model size, not to actual weight drift.

## Suggestion

A bucketed delta mode would remove most of this cost:

- hash/checksum per parameter bucket, sync only buckets whose checksum changed (in practice almost none change every step in RL fine-tuning — the update is small relative to init)

items.author: Davida1999
items.summary: Before the first rollout, Vime verifies that the trainer can restore the target-model parameters originally loaded by each vLLM endpoint. This check assumes that the trainer and rollout engines start from the same logical checkpoint.
items.body:
## Purpose

Implement the existing `--check-weight-update-equal` flag for the first actor-to-rollout weight update. Before the first rollout, Vime verifies that the trainer can restore the target-model parameters originally loaded by each vLLM endpoint. This check assumes that the trainer and rollout engines start from the same logical checkpoint.

Resetting the parameters before the update makes a missed transfer observable: if an update skips a previously nonzero tensor, its digest will differ from the saved baseline. See [RFC #537](https://github.com/vllm-project/vime/issues/537).

The NVLS AllGather-V and ReduceScatter-V kernels, and the ordered ReduceScatter-V used by batch-invariant mode, returned before their barrier when a CTA's `pid >= ep_max_tokens`. items.author: Doublrest
items.summary: In V1 trainers ( and ), whitens advantages once over the full sampled batch, whereas splits the batch into optimizer chunks without re-normalizing per chunk. When the sampled batch is larger than, individual optimizer chunks can have non-zero token-weighted ad…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8766.

In V1 trainers (`sync` and `colocate_async`), `_compute_advantage()` whitens advantages once over the full sampled batch, whereas `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()` splits the batch into `ppo_mini_batch_size` optimizer chunks without re-normalizing per chunk. When the sampled batch is larger than `ppo_mini_batch_size`, individual optimizer chunks can have non-zero token-weighted advantage means, introducing chunk-level policy-gradient drift.

This PR re-normalizes `mini_batch_td["advantages"]` per optimizer chunk in `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()`

items.author: AmineDiro
items.summary: On verl v0.9.1, verl's own Qwen2-7B-Instruct GRPO GSM8K recipe (the baseline in ) crashed twice on 8x B200, both times on the first training step after a validation pass. Right before the crash, the agent-loop workers log and carry on.
items.body:
## Summary

On verl v0.9.1, verl's own Qwen2-7B-Instruct GRPO GSM8K recipe (the `qwen2-7b-fsdp2.log` baseline in `docs/algo/baseline.md`) crashed twice on 8x B200, both times on the first training step after a validation pass. Right before the crash, the agent-loop workers log `Timeout waiting for data status update ACK from controller after 30s` and carry on. The data was written to storage but the controller never marks it ready, so the trainer later gets an empty batch from TransferQueue and fails with `KeyError: 'loss_mask'` in `compute_log_prob`.

The timeout itself is a slow controller.

items.title: [algo, trainer, fsdp, megatron, cfg, doc] feat: add topk_rb KL loss (top-k Rao-Blackwellised KL to the reference)
items.author: hiddevandebeek
items.summary: It adds, a KL penalty against the reference policy for. The estimator computes KL(πθ ‖ πref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Implements the RFC in #8536. It adds `actor.kl_loss_type: topk_rb`, a KL penalty against the reference policy for `use_kl_loss=True`.

The estimator computes KL(π_θ ‖ π_ref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket. The within-tail part is estimated from the sampled token, so the result is an **unbiased** estimate of the full-vocabulary KL gradient at every k, with much lower variance than the single-sample `kl`/`k2`/`low_var_kl`/`k3+` options. It is the per-token Rao-Blackwellised KL of [Amini et al., NeurIPS 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.1063

### What does this PR do?

Preserve vLLM's `finish_reason="length"` in `TokenOutput.stop_reason`. Today the vLLM rollout server reports `completed` both when generation stops naturally and when the output budget cuts it off. A caller translating this value to the Anthropic Messages API consequently sends `end_turn` for a truncated response, and the client can exit with work still in progress.

### Design and compatibility

Map vLLM's `stop` to `completed` and let `length` pass through the existing fallback. Callers can now return `max_tokens` to Anthropic clients. Abort still maps to `aborted`

items.title: [reward] fix: compare prime_code call-based outputs as plain builtins
items.author: Aarav500
items.summary: In, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of or whose always returns got full reward on every call-based task.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8656. In `prime_code`, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with `output == expected`. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of `int` or `list` whose `__eq__` always returns `True` got full reward on every call-based task. Swapping the operands doesn't help, because Python tries a subclass's reflected `__eq__` first.

This adds `_to_builtin()` in `prime_code/testing_util.py` and applies it to the output right after the existing `json.dumps(output)` call. It rebuilds the value from plain `None`/`bool`/`int`/`float

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

#8498 (`[megatron] feat: add TileLang FP8 and FP4 QAT kernels`) changed how weights are quantized before being synced to the rollout engine. For FP8_BLOCK, weights on GPU are now quantized by TileLang kernels instead of compressed-tensors (`verl/utils/qat/compressed_tensors.py`, `_compress_weight`):

```python
if weight.is_cuda and preset == ("FP8_BLOCK", None):

items.title: perf(r3): avoid full-size copies in routed-experts validation
items.author: dogeONE-bit
items.summary: On the default transport, which all R3 recipes under use, this loop runs serially in the after generation and before can start. The manager is a Ray actor, so Ray sets and torch runs the check on one thread.
items.body:
## Problem

With `--use-rollout-routing-replay`, `BatchBuilder.convert` runs `validate_routed_experts_tensor` on every sample that carries routes. On the default `object-store` transport, which all R3 recipes under `scripts/` use, this loop runs serially in the `RolloutManager` after generation and before `train()` can start. The manager is a `num_cpus=1` Ray actor, so Ray sets `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1` and torch runs the check on one thread. With straw, the same check runs per sample when groups are published (`SampleCodec._prepare_sample`).

items.summary: The engine now owns a device-bound NCCLGroup specialization with a single-device barrier and a logical group key shared across masked/shared ordinal layouts. Allocation, executor-thread broadcast, synchronization and destruction use the engine device.
items.body:
## Problem and behavior

Checkpoint participants each own one GPU, but Ray's default first barrier can enroll every visible GPU and its rendezvous key contains the local ordinal. The engine now owns a device-bound NCCLGroup specialization with a single-device barrier and a logical group key shared across masked/shared ordinal layouts. Allocation, executor-thread broadcast, synchronization and destruction use the engine device. Ordinary Ray groups retain their behavior, and duplicate ownership/topology checks remain. Delta transfers reuse this group and device without changing the wire protocol

items.author: R0k1e
items.summary: upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with, so the whole logits tensor is copied to fp32.
items.body:
## Motivation

`Float16Module.forward` upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with `labels=None`, so the whole `[T, V]` logits tensor is copied to fp32. The LM head GEMM has already rounded these values to bf16, so the copy adds memory but no precision. It is the largest single allocation in a long-context actor step: 40,960 tokens × 248,320 vocabulary is about 41 GB in fp32 versus 20 GB in bf16.

The fp32 copy does one useful thing: every consumer of the logits computes in fp32 because its input is fp32. This PR keeps that guarantee, but enforces it

## Problem

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

items.title: fix(data): give uniform reward groups exactly zero advantage
items.author: saloni-garg
items.summary: When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about …
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-
discussion: The nonzero advantages for uniform fractional rewards reproduce on `main`. I ran the grouped-reward tests at `0063710` on CPU with PyTorch 2.13.0: uniform groups produce exact zeros, and the mixed-group and nonfinite-reward cases pass too.
Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

`RayTrainGroup.create()` allocates training actors sequentially, discovers the rank-0 rendezvous address, initializes every actor, and optionally attaches the rollout manager.

A failure at any of those stages left already-created actors alive. Rank 0 was especially vulnerable because it was added to `_actor_handlers` only after its rendezvous lookup succeeded. The non-empty handler list also prevented a clean retry.

## Solution

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

## Background

## Solution

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

## Approach

## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | -0.1106 | -0.1111 | -0.1471 |
| After | -0.1088 | -0.1421 | -0.1

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

items.author: Xuan-1998
items.summary: The zero propagates into Megatron's, which fails during actor bring-up with a bare at (, no message). Nothing in the traceback points at the slime config knobs that caused it.
items.body:
## What this fixes

Launching training with a rollout configuration whose total sample count is smaller than the global batch size, for example:

```
--num-rollout 2 --rollout-batch-size 8 --n-samples-per-prompt 8 --global-batch-size 256
```

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

## Fix

Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. ## Background

In the agentic rollout path, each agent turn sends a request to SGLang through the SGLang router. When a request is cancelled or hits the client-side read timeout, Slime must explicitly abort the corresponding SGLang request to release its scheduler slot and KV-cache resources.

## Problem

`sglang_url` points to the SGLang router address, but the router does not expose or forward the `/abort_request` endpoint.

The existing cleanup logic sends:
